feature: Tool bar menus and Ask's photo row, from the walks that failed in the sweep
summary: The menus over the tool bar (Measure's Show, the Lens tool's kind, the Component tool's component) now wear the panel's own dropdown, and Measure's Snap there is the same two-part switch as in the panel. Ask's row says the kind of picture it made again ('Made a photo of a red fox'), not the request read back.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default.

try.do: Open a picture, press the Measure tool's key, and look at the bar over the tools: Snap is two buttons, Show is a dropdown.
try.shotNote: The window was behind another app when this was taken, so the picked half of Snap shows grey instead of the accent.

try.do: Click Show over the tool bar and pick Spacing; the panel's Show row reads Spacing too.
Open the Library's Comps, press N, and click the Component menu over the tool bar; pick Card.
Pick the Lens tool and choose its kind from the menu over the tool bar.
In a blank picture, ask 'make vector art of a fox', then ask 'as a photo'.
Read the newest row in the Agent section: it says 'Made a photo of' and the animal, in lower case, in whole words.

evaluate: Do the menus over the tool bar look like the panel's dropdowns, and does a click anywhere on one open it?
Is Snap as two buttons over the tool bar better than the menu it was?
After 'as a photo', does the Agent row say what you got, in words you would use?
While a photo is being made, does the progress line read naturally ('Making a photo of a red fox')?
rough: The Ask row takes the photo's subject from the model's own prompt, so it can say 'a red fox' when you asked for 'a fox'; it is cut at the first 'standing', 'in' or comma, never part way through a word.
No mock draws the bar over the tool bar with these menus; it now matches the panel's own rows for the same settings.

In a scripted walk, the title bar's View | Edit chip came out grey in dark when the recording was the first window opened; whether a person can ever see that is filed as find-out-whether-the-view-edit-switch-s-picked-c.
